instructions: At least 2 hours before you want them, or the day before you bake for the week: stir the 4 cups flour, 3/4 tsp salt and the packet of yeast together in a large bowl and make a well in the middle.

Crack 2 of the eggs into another bowl. Separate the third egg, adding the yolk to the bowl and keeping the white in a cup for later. Whisk in the 2 tbsp sugar, 3/4 cup yogurt and 1/4 cup lukewarm water.
Pour the egg mixture into the flour and stir until it comes together as a soft, sticky dough. Transfer it onto a floured counter and knead for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's smooth.
Rub the 1 tsp oil around a clean bowl, put the dough in and cover it tightly. Leave it somewhere warm until it's about doubled, 45 to 60 minutes.
Meanwhile, crumble the block of feta into a bowl. Finely chop 1/2 cup of the parsley leaves and mix them in with the 1/4 tsp pepper.
Line a large baking sheet with parchment. Turn the dough out, cut it into 8 even pieces and roll each into a ball. Cover them with a damp towel and let them rest for 5 minutes.

Press one ball out into an oval about 1/4 inch thick. Put an eighth of the feta in the middle, fold the dough over into a half moon and press the edge firmly with the side of your hand to seal it. Set it on the sheet and shape the rest.
Whisk the saved egg white with the 1 tbsp milk, brush it over the tops and scatter on the 2 tbsp sesame seeds. Leave them to puff up for 15 to 20 minutes while the oven heats to 350°F.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until they're deep golden on top and underneath. Cool them on a rack.
Serve them warm or at room temperature. Once they're cool, keep them in a tin or a bag for up to 3 days, or freeze them for a month. Warm them in a 350°F oven for 5 to 10 minutes.
advance_prep_notes: Bake ahead for the week: the dough rises for about an hour, so start at least 2 hours before. They keep 3 days in a tin or a month in the freezer.
method_notes: Both read versions fill a soft enriched dough with crumbled feta and parsley, brush the tops with egg and scatter on seeds before baking. Sainsbury's Magazine makes a quick yogurt and egg dough with fast action yeast, one long rise and a short second proof, and folds six large half moons; Cooking Gorgeous uses a milk, water and oil dough for 22 smaller buns and binds the filling with egg white. This follows Sainsbury's, scaled to 8 rolls. Neither version had 20 or more ratings (Sainsbury's has 19) and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for Turkish, has no version, so the best rated read version leads.
